items.claim: The 18:10-18:11 pairing is genuinely cohesive: the strength-noun root (עֹ֭ז/עֻזּ֑וֹ) and the exalted/safe root (וְנִשְׂגָּֽב/נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה) both recur across the seam in a deliberate antithetic construction contrasting YHWH's name as true refuge with the rich man's wealth as an imagined one.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms BYTE tier for all five pointed quotes against oshb:Prov.18.10 and oshb:Prov.18.11 ("מִגְדַּל עֹ֭ז"; "וְנִשְׂגָּֽב"; "קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ"; "נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה"; "בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ"); the row's bare root labels are correctly disclosed as skeleton-tier mentions rather than passed off as pointed quotes.

items.claim: The 18:18-18:19 pairing is a genuine catchword chain: the plural noun מִ֭דְיָנִים ("contentions") in 18:18 recurs exactly at the qere tier of 18:19's disclosed K/Q pair, correctly distinguished from its ketiv spelling ומדונים.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms BYTE tier for all four quotes against oshb:Prov.18.18 and oshb:Prov.18.19; pmarks_Prov.json kq inventory lists Prov.18.19 (count 1), matching the row's disclosed K/Q; the inline-ketiv hazard (unpointed ketiv token preceding the pointed qere in the same source string) is handled correctly, not conflated or miscounted.

items.claim: The row's rejected_alternative asserts a shared Hebrew root between 18:20 and 18:21 ("root shared... different body-part") but supplies zero Hebrew quotation and no oshb: citation anywhere in the row, an insufficient-engagement defect even though the underlying fact is byte-true.
items.evidence: verse_map_oshb.json shows the shared root is the fruit-noun: 18:20 מִפְּרִ֣י (from-fruit-of, mouth/lips) vs 18:21 פִּרְיָֽהּ (its fruit, tongue) - a real pointed-root match the row never quotes or cites at any tier; boundary_evidence_refs carries only web: entries, no oshb: entry at all, despite the claim resting on a Hebrew lexical fact.
tier_citations: none: no Hebrew quote or oshb: citation present in the row despite an OL-dependent claim

items.claim: device_notes calls Prov.19.22 an echo of the "same opening formula" as the verse-initial tov-openers at 17:1/19:1, but 19:22's first skeleton token is תַּאֲוַ֣ת, not ט֤וֹב - the tov-token opens only 19:22's second colon, so 19:22 is not a member of the 16-verse verse-initial tov_openers set the row otherwise cites correctly.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.19.22 text "תַּאֲוַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְטֽוֹב רָ֝שׁ מֵאִ֥ישׁ כָּזָֽב" has the tov-token as word 4 (second-colon opener), not word 1; prov_device_inventory.json tov_openers.refs (count 16, first-skeleton-token test) excludes Prov.19.22 while including Prov.17.1 and Prov.19.1, confirming the row's own two genuine citations but not the third. Does not disturb the row's single_proverb decision, which the 16-verse sweep digit otherwise supports.

items.claim: The row's entire justification for declining a cluster with 19:1 is "see that row's disclosure" - a positional cross-reference rather than verse-anchored evidence - so read on its own bytes the row carries zero Hebrew engagement of the shared טֽוֹב token its own decision turns on.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.19.1 ("טֽוֹב", verse-initial comparative) and oshb:Prov.19.2 ("לֹא ט֑וֹב", mid-verse "not good" predicate) do share the exact token in different syntactic roles - the same distinction row P08-050 draws for itself - but P08-051 states none of it independently; the campaign register bars positional/file-order cross-references in row prose, and this row's rejected_alternative is exactly that, leaving its own boundary claim unevidenced in isolation.
tier_citations: byte:oshb:Prov.19.2 (shared token, undisclosed in this row's own text)

items.claim: The row correctly identifies 19:5 and 19:9 as a near-verbatim doublet that cannot cluster because the two verses are non-adjacent, though its "opening colon" description understates the match, which extends (at the accent-stripped tier) through the first half of colon 2 as well before the two verses diverge at the closing clause.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.19.5 "עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט" and oshb:Prov.19.9 "עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֖יחַ כְּזָבִ֣ים יֹאבֵֽד" are BYTE-identical for all of colon 1, "עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה"; colon 2's opening two words (וְיָפִ֥יחַ/וְיָפִ֖יחַ, כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים/כְּזָבִ֣ים) match only at the ACCENT-STRIPPED tier (same consonants+vowels, different cantillation), not byte-for-byte; full divergence begins at the closing clause (לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט vs יֹאבֵֽד). Non-adjacency (19:6-19:8 intervene) correctly bars any cluster regardless of match extent, so the boundary call is sound despite the understatement and despite this correction to the row's own would-be tier.

items.claim: The friend-root the row treats as a distinctive two-verse elaboration binding 19:6-19:7 also occurs, undisclosed, in 19:4 (רֵעִ֣ים, מֵרֵ֥עהוּ) - three hits across a four-verse span with a gap only at 19:5 - which weakens the claim that the repetition is a deliberate pairing device rather than the book's ordinary weak-local-cohesion vocabulary texture.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.19.4 "ה֗וֹן יֹ֭סִיף רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝דָ֗ל מֵרֵ֥עהוּ יִפָּרֵֽד" carries the same pointed root (tsere, the companion sense, not the qamats "evil" homograph) as the row's own quotes at 19:6/19:7; the row's immediate seam neighbors 19:5 and 19:8 carry no such root, so this is chapter texture rather than a seam-adjacent violation, but it is a byte-true recurrence the row does not disclose. The row's own confidence is already medium_low and its fallback discourse-logic (a-fortiori dependency) argument is untouched by this finding.

items.claim: The row states the shared noun אִשָּׁ֥ה "closes the second colon of both verses" at "the same line-final slot," which is byte-true for 19:13 but not for 19:14, where the noun is followed by the adjective מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת and so is colon-medial, not colon-final.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.19.13 ends "מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה" (noun verse/colon-final) but oshb:Prov.19.14 ends "אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת" (noun followed by one more word). The antithetic wife-pairing and the shared-noun cohesion the row argues from remain byte-true and support the cluster; only the "closes"/"line-final" positional framing overreaches for 19:14.
